title: Mimesis: The Representation of Reality in Western Literature
author: Erich Auerbach
hint: This is less a plot to spoil than an argument about how literature learns to represent reality.
partial_spoiler: Auerbach moves across Western literature to show how style, history, class, and realism change across time.
full_spoiler: The book argues that Western literature gradually expands what can count as serious representation, making ordinary life, mixed styles, and historical reality central to literary art.
character_fates: No fictional character fate; the 'fate' here is realism becoming a historical method of seeing.

title: Recitatif
author: Toni Morrison
hint: The story withholds the very information readers are trained to search for.
partial_spoiler: Two women remember the same childhood institution and the same disabled woman differently, but race remains deliberately unstable.
full_spoiler: The story never reveals which girl is Black and which is white, forcing the reader to confront how racial assumptions are produced by reading itself.
character_fates: Twyla and Roberta survive into adulthood, but their shared memory of Maggie remains unresolved.

title: Geography III
author: Elizabeth Bishop
hint: The poems turn measurement into uncertainty.
partial_spoiler: Bishop uses maps, questions, and precise description to show how difficult it is to locate the self or the world securely.
full_spoiler: The collection keeps staging geography as a failed promise of orientation: description does not master the world, but reveals its instability.
character_fates: No character deaths; the speaker remains attentive, estranged, and unsettled.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
hint: The ending is domestic
partial_spoiler: but not simple.
full_spoiler: The sisters grow into separate lives, and one beloved sister does not survive.
character_fates: Beth dies, Amy marries Laurie, Jo does not marry Laurie and instead marries Professor Bhaer, later building a school.
ending_type: Beth dies; Jo marries Bhaer; Amy marries Laurie; Meg marries John Brooke.

title: The Portrait of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
hint: The portrait keeps the truth the body refuses.
partial_spoiler: Dorian remains outwardly beautiful while the hidden portrait records his corruption.
full_spoiler: Dorian tries to destroy the portrait, but kills himself instead; his body becomes aged and ruined while the portrait returns to beauty.
character_fates: Dorian dies; Basil is murdered by Dorian; Sibyl Vane dies by suicide.

title: The Bluest Eye
author: Toni Morrison
hint: The book asks what happens when beauty becomes a weapon.
partial_spoiler: Pecola is destroyed by racism, sexual violence, and the community's failure to protect her.
full_spoiler: Pecola is raped by her father, becomes pregnant, loses the baby, and retreats into delusion, believing she has blue eyes.
character_fates: Pecola survives physically but is psychologically shattered; her baby dies; Cholly dies.

title: Fun Home: A Family Tragicomic
author: Alison Bechdel
hint: The family home is both museum and evidence.
partial_spoiler: Bechdel connects her coming-out, her father's closeted sexuality, and his sudden death.
full_spoiler: Bruce Bechdel dies after being hit by a truck, and the memoir leaves open whether his death was accidental or suicide.
character_fates: Bruce Bechdel dies; Alison survives into authorship and interpretation.

title: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous
author: Ocean Vuong
hint: The book is a letter that knows it may never be fully received.
partial_spoiler: Little Dog writes to his mother about family history, violence, migration, language, and first love.
full_spoiler: Trevor dies of an overdose, and the novel ends as a meditation on memory, survival, inheritance, and the limits of address.
character_fates: Trevor dies; Little Dog survives through writing; Rose and Lan remain central presences in memory.

title: Play It As It Lays
author: Joan Didion
hint: The plot feels like a life stripped of explanation.
partial_spoiler: Maria drifts through Hollywood, emotional numbness, abortion, failed relationships, and institutionalization.
full_spoiler: Maria ends in a psychiatric facility, still refusing easy meaning, while BZ dies by suicide after asking her to stay with him.
character_fates: BZ dies by suicide; Maria survives but remains emotionally detached and institutionalized.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
hint: This is not love as cure
partial_spoiler: but love as haunting.
full_spoiler: Catherine dies, Heathcliff becomes consumed by revenge, and the next generation suffers from the first generation's violence.
character_fates: Catherine dies after marrying Edgar; Heathcliff destroys several lives through revenge, then dies obsessed with Catherine's ghost. Cathy and Hareton finally suggest a gentler future.
ending_type: Catherine dies; Heathcliff dies; Hindley dies; Linton dies; Cathy and Hareton survive together.

title: Monolingualism of the Other
author: Jacques Derrida
hint: The book begins from an impossible claim about language and belonging.
partial_spoiler: Derrida argues that the language one calls one's own is always inherited from elsewhere.
full_spoiler: The book unsettles the idea of native language by showing how language, identity, colonial history, and origin are never fully possessed.
character_fates: No character fate; the stable subject of language is what gets undone.

title: The Virgin Suicides
author: Jeffrey Eugenides
hint: The title tells you the ending
partial_spoiler: but not the meaning.
full_spoiler: All five Lisbon sisters die by suicide, while the neighborhood boys remain unable to understand them.
character_fates: Cecilia dies first, and the remaining sisters later die in a coordinated sequence, leaving the male narrators with obsession rather than understanding.
ending_type: Cecilia, Lux, Bonnie, Mary, and Therese Lisbon all die by suicide.

title: Last Looks, Last Books
author: Helen Vendler
hint: The book studies how poets write when lateness becomes visible.
partial_spoiler: Vendler reads late poetry by major poets as a record of endings, revisions, and final styles.
full_spoiler: The central revelation is critical rather than narrative: late style becomes a way of confronting death, form, and the last possible gestures of art.
character_fates: No fictional fate; the book is concerned with poetic mortality.

title: My Year of Rest and Relaxation
author: Ottessa Moshfegh
hint: Sleep becomes less escape than experiment.
partial_spoiler: The narrator attempts to drug herself into a year of near-total sleep, while her friendship with Reva deteriorates.
full_spoiler: After the narrator emerges from her hibernation, Reva dies in the September 11 attacks, and the narrator watches footage of a falling woman she imagines as Reva.
character_fates: Reva dies in 9/11; the narrator survives changed but not cleanly redeemed.

title: Amy Foster
author: Joseph Conrad
hint: The tragedy begins with not being understood.
partial_spoiler: Yanko survives a shipwreck and marries Amy, but remains isolated by language and xenophobia.
full_spoiler: When Yanko becomes ill and speaks in his native language, Amy fears him and abandons him; he dies isolated.
character_fates: Yanko dies; Amy survives but becomes part of the story's failure of sympathy.

title: Bunny
author: Mona Awad
hint: The workshop is more dangerous than it looks.
partial_spoiler: Samantha is drawn into a cultish writing group whose rituals blur art, violence, and fantasy.
full_spoiler: The Bunnies conjure hybrid boys through ritual, and the novel leaves reality unstable as Samantha confronts Ava, creativity, loneliness, and monstrosity.
character_fates: Ava's reality is uncertain; Samantha survives but remains inside ambiguity.

title: Set My Heart on Fire
author: Izumi Suzuki
hint: Coolness keeps turning into danger.
partial_spoiler: The stories often follow women navigating alienation, desire, passivity, and social worlds that punish detachment.
full_spoiler: Rather than building to one plot ending, the collection repeatedly reveals how emotional distance can become its own trap.
character_fates: Varies by story; the recurring fate is stylish disillusionment rather than rescue.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
hint: The ghost is not only a ghost.
partial_spoiler: Sethe's dead daughter returns in embodied form, forcing the household to confront the violence of slavery and memory.
full_spoiler: Sethe killed her child rather than let her be returned to slavery; Beloved appears as that dead daughter, then vanishes after the women of the community intervene.
character_fates: Beloved vanishes; Sethe survives; Denver steps into the world; Paul D returns.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
hint: The romance has a locked room inside it.
partial_spoiler: Rochester is already married to Bertha Mason, who is hidden in the attic.
full_spoiler: Jane leaves after discovering Bertha, later returns after Thornfield burns, Bertha dies, and Rochester is injured. Jane marries him on more equal terms.
character_fates: Bertha dies; Rochester is blinded and maimed; Jane survives and marries Rochester.

title: Rebecca
author: Daphne du Maurier
hint: The dead wife controls the house more than the living one.
partial_spoiler: Rebecca was not the perfect wife everyone imagines, and Maxim's grief is not what it seems.
full_spoiler: Maxim killed Rebecca after she manipulated him into believing she was pregnant; Manderley is later burned by Mrs. Danvers.
character_fates: Rebecca is already dead; Mrs. Danvers likely burns Manderley; Maxim and the narrator survive in exile.

title: The Secret History
author: Donna Tartt
hint: The murder is not the mystery; the aftermath is.
partial_spoiler: The group kills Bunny because he knows too much about an earlier death.
full_spoiler: The classics students accidentally kill a farmer during a bacchanal, then murder Bunny to hide it. Henry later dies by suicide.
character_fates: Bunny is murdered; Henry dies by suicide; the others survive damaged and scattered.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
hint: The school is preparing the students for a future already decided for them.
partial_spoiler: Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy are clones raised to donate organs.
full_spoiler: There is no deferral for love; Ruth and Tommy complete their donations and die, while Kathy awaits the same fate.
character_fates: Ruth dies; Tommy dies; Kathy survives temporarily but is expected to donate.

title: Giovanni's Room
author: James Baldwin
hint: The room becomes a place of desire and refusal.
partial_spoiler: David abandons Giovanni because he cannot face what their relationship means for his identity.
full_spoiler: Giovanni is executed for murder after David leaves him, and David ends alone, haunted by cowardice and desire.
character_fates: Giovanni is executed; David survives in guilt; Hella leaves.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
hint: The dream is built on a woman who cannot bear its weight.
partial_spoiler: Daisy kills Myrtle while driving Gatsby's car, and Gatsby takes the blame.
full_spoiler: George Wilson kills Gatsby, believing he caused Myrtle's death. Daisy and Tom leave, and almost no one attends Gatsby's funeral.
character_fates: Gatsby dies; Myrtle dies; George dies; Daisy and Tom leave unharmed.

title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
author: Zora Neale Hurston
hint: Love arrives
partial_spoiler: but not without a storm.
full_spoiler: Janie finds love with Tea Cake, but the hurricane changes everything.
character_fates: Tea Cake contracts rabies after saving Janie, becomes violent, and Janie kills him in self-defense. She returns home with her story.
ending_type: Tea Cake dies; Janie survives and returns with self-knowledge.

title: Wide Sargasso Sea
author: Jean Rhys
hint: This is the story behind the woman in the attic.
partial_spoiler: Antoinette is renamed Bertha by Rochester and gradually loses autonomy, home, and identity.
full_spoiler: Antoinette is taken to England and confined in the attic, where the ending points toward the fire that will destroy Thornfield in Jane Eyre.
character_fates: Antoinette is imprisoned and moves toward self-destruction; Rochester survives into Jane Eyre's plot.

title: Passing
author: Nella Larsen
hint: The danger is not only being seen
partial_spoiler: but being read correctly.
full_spoiler: Clare passes as white, reenters Irene's life, and destabilizes her marriage and sense of safety.
character_fates: Clare falls from a window after her racist husband discovers her racial identity; the novel leaves ambiguous whether Irene pushed her, failed to save her, or merely witnessed it.
ending_type: Clare dies; Irene survives inside ambiguity; Brian's future remains uncertain.

title: Mrs. Dalloway
author: Virginia Woolf
hint: A party and a death happen in the same day.
partial_spoiler: Clarissa prepares for a party while Septimus, a traumatized veteran, moves toward suicide.
full_spoiler: Septimus kills himself by jumping from a window to avoid psychiatric confinement, and Clarissa hears of his death during her party, interpreting it as a profound act of refusal.
character_fates: Septimus dies by suicide; Clarissa survives and returns to the party.

title: The Bell Jar
author: Sylvia Plath
hint: The descent is psychological
partial_spoiler: not melodramatic.
full_spoiler: Esther spirals into depression, attempts suicide, and is institutionalized.
character_fates: Esther survives her suicide attempt and treatment, but the ending remains uncertain as she prepares for an interview about release.
ending_type: Esther survives; Joan dies by suicide.

title: The Handmaid's Tale
author: Margaret Atwood
hint: The ending refuses to tell you whether escape is rescue.
partial_spoiler: Offred is taken away in a van that may belong to the Eyes or the resistance.
full_spoiler: Offred's fate is left unresolved; the epilogue reveals her story survives as historical testimony studied after Gilead falls.
character_fates: Offred's fate is unknown; Gilead eventually falls; her narrative survives.
